newsitem.title: USA: US stocks fall as computer chip shares sink.
newsitem.headline: US stocks fall as computer chip shares sink.

text.p: Stocks fell Tuesday despite a surge in bonds, as semiconductor shares tumbled after an earnings warning from Xilinx Inc. raised alarms for the entire industry.
"The market is struggling," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.
"We finished end-of-quarter window-dressing and I wouldn't be surprised if after the run we've had over the past week or two if we took a pause over the next few days."

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 16.77 points to 5,865.40. In the broader market, advancing issues were about even with declining ones on volume of 236 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The technology-studded Nasdaq Composite index lost 11.04 points or 0.90 percent to 1,215.88. The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's semiconductor index slumped 5.64 points, or 3.01 percent, to 181.82.

Xilinx, which supplies programmable logic devices to the phone and data networking industries, shed 2-3/4 to 31-1/4 after forecasting net income and revenue for the second quarter ended Sept. 28 would be below first quarter results. UBS Securities downgraded the stock to hold from buy, while other brokers slashed earnings estimates.
Among other chip stocks, Atmel lost 1-9/16 to 29-5/16, Lattice Semiconductor fell 1 to 27-7/8 and Altera eased 5/8 to 50.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond climbed 13/32, knocking its yield down to 6.89 percent from 6.92 percent at Monday's.

The National Association of Purchasing Management's index fell more than expected to 51.7 in September from 52.6 in August, signalling moderate economic growth and no extreme price pressures. A reading above 50 points to growth in manufacturing while one below that level signals contraction.
Separately, the Conference Board said its index of leading economic indicators posted a 0.2 percent rise for August, in line with economists' forecasts.

"We're probably starting off the fourth quarter thinking that bonds are going to do better than stocks because the economy is slowing down," said Tom Carpenter, chief economist at ASB Capital Management Inc.

"What you'll see (in the third quarter) is a clear drop in momentum for corporate earnings growth but it's important to understand that there's a great shock absorber for stocks in lower interest rates," he added.
Josephthal's Blumberg said, "I don't think we're finished with this advance (in stocks). We have more room to go on the upside and we're two-thirds through."

Among special situations, HCIA Inc. plummeted 46 percent or 27-1/2 points to 32-1/2 after warning that weak revenues would drag its earnings well below analysts' expectations. Merrill downgraded the stock.
Alex Brown cut HCIA to neutral from strong buy on the earnings warning and then restored its strong buy rating on the stock drop.

America Online lost 3-3/4 to 31-7/8 as investors reacted to the company's repeated warnings that other online services and direct Internet access providers could spell tougher future competition, industry analysts said.
